Robert Pape's newsletter last week
[ran](https://escalationtrap.substack.com/p/the-third-carrier-has-arrived-
trumps) a big scary headline: "The Third Carrier Has Arrived -- Trump's Strike
Window Is Open."

Translation: a third giant U.S. warship had shown up near Iran, virtual proof
that Trump was about to commence a massive invasion. But a week later, one of
the aircraft carriers returned home. No invasion.

What happened?

If you don't know Robert Pape, you've probably still seen him. He's a
professor who TV shows and newspapers love having on to talk about the Iran
War. His fancy title gives them cover for Alex Jones-level headlines like
"Many Will Die," which actually ran on PBS's _Amanpour and Company_ (see
screenshot below).

On paper, Robert Pape is exactly the kind of expert Washington is always
telling you to trust. He's a Truman Scholar with a PhD from the University of
Chicago. He taught at Dartmouth, then went back to Chicago, where he's now a
tenured professor of political science and runs a research center on security
threats.

In practice, he's a tent-revival preacher in a sharp suit, barking about the
end times.

Since Trump launched the Iran War at the end of February, Pape has been
preaching the gospel of the "escalation trap," the theory that we're now
locked into a practically inevitable spiral of military escalation against
Iran. Where an end-of-days preacher would speak in tongues, he speaks in
Latin, peppering interviews with terms like "_casus belli_." And like every
doomsday prophet, he keeps getting the date wrong.

So when a third aircraft carrier pulled into the region last week,
professional prophets like Pape got right to work, supplying the media with
its usual quota of panic.

The news media piled on. OMG! Aircraft carrier means 55,000 troops in the
region! More than ever! Iranian dirty bomb! WMD!

What you'd have to dig to page 3,000 to find is that within days of the
Roosevelt's arrival, the USS George Washington [left the Middle
East](https://news.usni.org/2026/11/18/carrier-uss-george-washington-leaves-
middle-east-after-three-months) and sailed back to Japan. Home for the
holidays.

If you're wondering why you heard all about the three-carrier buildup but
nothing about it ending, look at how little attention the media gave it.

The Washington Post, which had run its own three-carrier story, covered the
departure with a short AP wire item: "[US military returns to 2 aircraft
carriers in the Middle
East](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/11/18/iran-war-aircraft-
carrier-uss-george-
washington/7edaf88e-e39d-11f1-a99e-b3e3805c6b8b_story.html)." Bloomberg's
[departure story](https://bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-18/us-carrier-
leaves-persian-gulf-for-japan-leaving-two-in-region) led readers back to the
threat, claiming that somehow the Roosevelt gave Trump more military options.
CBS News buried the departure in a [live blog](https://www.cbsnews.com/live-
updates/iran-war-us-gulf-retaliation-strikes-strait-of-hormuz/) saying that
Tehran may still be working on chemical or biological weapons. And no outlets
seemed much interested in President Trump's post-midterm admission that the
war "is effectively over."

The media would not have had to look far to learn that the third aircraft
carrier was sent over not as some kind of operatic buildup to total war, but
simply to take the George Washington's place. Back in September, USNI News,
the U.S. Naval Institute's news site,
[reported](https://news.usni.org/?p=125507) that the Roosevelt had left San
Diego to relieve the George Washington. That's how carrier rotations work
(especially amid holidays): the new ship shows up, the two overlap briefly,
and the old one leaves. The same thing happened in August, when the George
Washington replaced the Abraham Lincoln.

And as for the 55,000 troops figure, the media makes it seem as if Marines are
chomping at the bit. The reality? That includes everyone: not just warfighters
but cooks, logistics, intel people, and on and on.

* * *

The trouble with Pape's "escalation trap" theory is that it assumes escalation
is inevitable. If war is inevitable, nobody has the agency (or responsibility)
to stop it: not Trump, not the Israelis, not Hegseth, and not the Pentagon
bureaucrats shuffling carriers around on a schedule.  
  
The real escalation trap is the media hype cycle. Its entire incentive
structure is built around promising big explosions. There is an endless market
for telling people it's DEFCON 1, that war is imminent, that the countdown has
begun, that the fuse is lit -- and almost no reward for telling them that
nothing happened, or that the military quietly stood down.

Once outlets and pundits crank the dial to red, they can't turn it back down
without losing the audience's attention. Every routine deployment has to be
framed as the prelude to a massive strike; every quiet de-escalation gets
buried or ignored. The result is an information ecosystem permanently locked
on the brink of war, where the only story worth telling is that the next
explosion is just around the corner -- even as the warships are literally
sailing away.

Pape will presumably cram Iran into his next book as proof his theory works,
whether or not the real world cooperates.

The real story is actually an encouraging one: millions of ordinary Americans
voted against the Iran War so decisively that they stood up to the Pentagon
and won.
